conversation.Statement: Hello, this is Agent Michael Newman from the IRS Tax Refund Department. I'm calling regarding your recent self-employment tax filings. May I confirm that I'm speaking with Alex Ramirez?
Yes, this is Alex. Um, what's this about? I drive for RideNow and deliver food sometimes, but I already filed my taxes.

Thank you, Alex. Our records indicate you're eligible for a federal stimulus refund due to overreported earnings on your 2023 gig income. This is part of a special IRS adjustment for independent contractors. Have you received any emails from us recently?
No, I haven't gotten anything from the IRS. Are you sure this is right? I thought I might actually owe money.

According to our system, there is a $1,127.40 refund ready for immediate disbursement. However, before we can release the funds, IRS policy requires identity confirmation and a processing fee to ensure the refund goes to the correct account holder.
Wait, I have to pay a fee to get my tax refund? I never heard of that before.

This is a new security protocol implemented because of the increased fraud involving gig workers' tax filings. The processing and identity verification fee is $98, which is fully reimbursed with your refund. This ensures your funds are not intercepted by unauthorized parties.
So I pay $98 now, and then I get the refund plus the fee back?

Correct. Once we confirm your identity and process the payment, the full $1,225.40 will be credited to your account within two business days. Without this, unfortunately, the IRS will be forced to place a hold on your refund due to incomplete verification.
That doesn't sound right. I've never had to do this before.

This is mandatory for all self-employed individuals flagged for manual review. If you decline, the IRS is required to suspend your refund and may initiate a compliance audit, which can lead to additional fines or penalties if discrepancies are found. We want to help you avoid that.
I really can't afford an audit or more penalties. How do I pay the fee?

For your convenience, you can complete the identity and processing fee via a secure Zelle transfer. Please send $98 to our official IRS processing payment handle: IRS-Refund-Dept-782. Do you have the Zelle app installed on your phone?
Yeah, I use Zelle sometimes. So I just send it to that username?

That's correct. Once you send the payment, please provide me with the confirmation code so I can process your refund. This must be completed within the next 30 minutes or the refund will be flagged as unclaimed.
Um, okay. Let me see if I have enough in my account.

If you do not have sufficient funds for Zelle, we can also accept Visa or Mastercard payment over the phone, or you may purchase a Vanilla prepaid card from any convenience store and provide the code. If payment is not received today, you may lose eligibility for the refund.
Is there really a deadline? I don't want to miss out, but this seems weird.

IRS guidelines are strict, refunds not claimed within the specified window are forfeited and may trigger further investigation. Please act quickly to avoid unnecessary complications or the possibility of incurring penalties for non-compliance.
Alright, I'll try Zelle. Just to be sure, is this really the IRS? I'm just worried, you know.

I understand your concern, Alex. This is an official IRS line and your case file number is 4812-RT. You can verify this after your refund is processed, but for now, prompt action is required to secure your funds.
Okay, I'll send the money. What do I do after I send it?
Once the $98 is sent via Zelle to IRS-Refund-Dept-782, please read me the transaction confirmation number. I will immediately finalize your refund and email you the confirmation receipt.
Alright, I'll do it now. Please wait a second.
Of course, I'm on the line. Please let me know as soon as you've completed the transfer so we can proceed.
